title: Overbrenging van het lijk van Napoleon Bonaparte van St. Helena naar Frankrijk
author: anonymous
description:
The medal titled "Overbrenging van het lijk van Napoleon Bonaparte van St. Helena naar Frankrijk," created anonymously in 1840, serves as a poignant commemoration of the transportation of Napoleon Bonaparte's remains from his exile on the island of St. Helena to France. The piece is a history medal, crafted using techniques of striking and gilding, showcasing both the artistry of metalworking and the significance of the historical event it represents.

On the obverse side of the medal, the finely executed relief depicts a solemn visage of Napoleon, identifiable by his distinctive features. Surrounding the portrait are inscriptions that denote his name and title, "NAPOLEON EMPEREUR," emphasizing his status and legacy. The reverse side of the medal inscribes the critical details of his death and the transfer of his remains, including the date of his passing on May 5, 1821, and the moment of his remains being returned to France on September 30, 1840. The use of gilding adds a striking quality to the metal, enhancing its historical significance and allowing it to shine as a cherished artifact reflecting a substantial moment in French history.

This medal not only highlights the reverence held for Napoleon long after his death but also embodies the broader themes of memory, honor, and the complex legacy of one of history's most prominent figures.
